66.01.additionalInfo: In Master Tung's book, translated into English, the point is numbered 66.01. For more information, see the numbering of the points. Master Tung used the point for pain in the thumb and the second finger, but Hu Wen Zhi uses the point for pain in all the fingers, similar to 11.27 Wu Hu, which is located on the thumb. Yang Wei Chieh The point innervates the heart. According to the Five Wheels of Eye Diagnosis, the corners of the eye are related to the heart, so the point can treat inflammation in the corner of the eye, which can spread from the edges to the entire eye, depending on the severity of the condition. The point is close to the Jing-Well point. Jing-Well points treat openings so that the point can be effective in treating vaginal discharge and conjunctivitis. Lee Kuo Cheng The point is close to Sp-l Yin Bair so like Sp-l, it can stop uterine bleeding. Originally, 100 small moxa cones were applied. Imaging Imaging between the upper and lower limbs: the toes represent the fingers, so the point can treat pain in the thumb. Point Name Häi Båo — to seal, to close. The name of the point suggests its ability to treat vaginal and uterine discharges.

66.02.additionalInfo: In Master Tung's book, which has been translated into English, the point is numbered 66.02. For more information, see the point numbering. This point innervates the heart and is called Mu (wood/liver). The heart governs the blood, and the liver stores the blood. 66.02 Mu fu treats gynecological disorders related to blood stagnation. Both 55.01 Huo bao and 66.02 Mu fu affect the heart and liver. The difference is that 66.02 Mu fu is located on the yang side of the second toe and innervates the six Fu organs (treating excess conditions) according to Hu Wen Zhi. Therefore, its ability to treat blood stagnation is stronger than 55.01 Huo bao, located on the yin side of the second toe. Thus, it has a stronger ability to treat liver and heart diseases. Susan Johnson Uses 66.02 Mu fu (55) to treat Interstitial Cystitis, especially in cases associated with anger and a burning sensation during urination. Point Name Mü [X] - wood, tree. Fü I"] — woman, married woman. The character "woman" in the name of the point suggests its ability to treat disorders in the female reproductive system. The character "wood" in the name of the point suggests its ability to treat disorders involving the liver.

66.04.additionalInfo: Sometimes, 66.03 Huo ying is combined with 66.04 Huo Zhu in the Dao ma technique. 66.03 Huo Ying and 66.04 Huo Zhu are points that innervate the heart. They can invigorate the blood, reduce swelling and heat, and break up stagnation, such as ovarian cysts and uterine fibroids. For these conditions, they can be combined with 77.05-07 San Zhong. Point Name Huö ['k] - fire. Zhü — lord, master. Huö - fire. The character "fire" in the point's name suggests its connection with the heart and the upper burner due to the upward movement of fire. Therefore, the point can treat heart diseases and head disorders. The character "master" in the name of the point hints at its influence on the heart (the emperor).

66.05.additionalInfo: 66.05 Men Jin is sometimes needled together with Men Jin Xia using the Dao Ma technique. 66.05 Men Jin affects the middle and lower burner and is an essential point for treating stomach, intestines, and reproductive disorders. The point also affects the head and can treat a wide range of headaches and migraines, temporomandibular joint syndrome (TMJ), nasal congestion, and trigeminal neuralgia. According to Li Jing-Xiong, needling the point toward Ki-1 Yong Quan treats vertex headaches. For pain and numbness in the middle finger, 66.05 Men Jin is combined with 66.06 Mu Liu. According to Chuan Min Wang, the point can treat temporal headaches. Point Name Mén [P f] — Gate. Jin [ft] — Metal. The character "metal" in the name of the point suggests its effect on the large intestine (metal). Mén [FY] — Gate. Jin — Metal. Points with the character "gate" in their name open and release stagnation and excess. In the case of 66.05 Men Jin, it refers to stagnation in the middle and lower burner.

66.07.additionalInfo: 66.06 Mu Liu is sometimes used together with 66.07 Mu Dou using the Dao Ma technique. These points innervate the spleen and liver and can, therefore, address imbalances between the spleen and liver, manifested in the following ways: Digestive disorders due to an imbalance between wood (liver) and earth (spleen). Due to their connection with the liver and spleen, they also treat blood disorders. In such cases, they can be combined with Tu Chang (88) and 88.12-14 Shang San Huang. Numbness throughout the body due to blood blockage and stagnation (the liver stores the blood, and the spleen governs the blood). It is interesting to compare with 22.10 Shou Jie, which treats numbness, but in this case, the cause is the heart, which controls the blood. The points treat chronic fatigue syndrome due to over-control of wood over the earth. Stiffness of the tongue after a stroke. These points can be used for liver wind disorders characterized by mild or severe involuntary tremors affecting the hands, legs, face, and tongue. The points can also treat pain and stiffness in the third and fourth fingers due to the correlation between the fingers of the hands and the toes. When treating Morton's neuroma, needle on the affected side. Chuan Min Wang A case of Master Tung: Rhinitis, needling of 66.06-07 Mu Liu/Dou to treat nasal blockage. Master Tung thought, "Strengthen the earth (spleen) to produce metal (lungs)." A case of Master Tung: Pain on the lateral side of both arms. Master Tung believed that the root of the problem was the spleen, which governs the four limbs, so he needled 66.06 Mu Liu. Lai Jing Xiong Used 66.06-07 Mu Liu/Dou for clavicle swelling. After one visit, the swelling decreased, and after eight visits, the swelling completely disappeared. Point Name Mü Wood. Döu Ladle, bucket, measuring instrument. The character "wood" suggests that the point affects the liver, while the character "bucket" implies something that has accumulated and the point's ability to treat an enlarged spleen. If the hand radical is added to "Dou", it becomes the character "Dou" [94], which means "tremor." This suggests the point's ability to treat liver-related wind disorders. The Big Dipper is called "Bei Dou Xing" [ l. The character "Dou" [ 1 in the point's name suggests its connection to the Big Dipper. In Chinese cosmology, the Big Dipper is located at the center of the Sky. The center is associated with the Earth, so the point's name hints at its connection with the Earth. In summary, the point's name suggests something stuck in the spleen and liver. In the case of the spleen, the wood that controls the earth releases the stagnation.

66.11.additionalInfo: Some sources place 66.11 Huo Ju at the same location as Sp-4 Gong Sun. This point is particularly useful for treating frontal headaches, mainly when the pain is above the eye. Yang Wei Chieh To accelerate weight loss, it is recommended to needle Si-4 Wan Gu, 66.11 Huo Ju, 77.14 Si Hua Wait St-34 Liang Qiu, and Cv-4 Guan Yuan. For additional information, see 66.12 Huo San. Point Name Huö — Fire. Jü [5] — Chrysanthemum. Huö ['k] — Fire. The character "Fire" in the point's name suggests its connection to the heart and its ability to clear fire. Chuan Min Wang Since the chrysanthemum is an autumn herb, and autumn is the season of harvest in Chinese medicine, Chuan Min Wang believes that the point's name can be interpreted as "Gathering Fire." This name more accurately describes the point's function alongside the other two points in this group: 66.10 "Connecting Fire" and 66.12 "Dispersing Fire." The inclusion of "Chrysanthemum" in the point's name reflects its similarity to the herb Ju Hua. The point and the herb have similar properties; they treat excess heat and wind in the head region.

66.12.additionalInfo: Some sources place 66.12 Huo San at the exact location as Kid-2 Ran Gu. It is common to use the Dao Ma technique to needle 66.10 Huo Lian, 66.11 Huo Ju, and 66.12 Huo San together. When needled together, they are called Zu San Huo [ Z 'k J, the "Three Fires of the Leg." Combining these three points can treat excess fire (Yang) in the upper body, such as hypertension, dizziness, palpitations, insomnia, and meningitis. The points are innervated by the heart and kidney channels and address the lack of communication between the heart and kidneys, which leads to excess fire in the upper body (water controlling fire). Master Tung wrote in his book that the three points can be used to treat brain tumors and meningitis (needling on one side only). This combination can also treat a fire deficiency (circulation) in the upper body, such as hair loss, scalp itching, and deficiency-induced dizziness. Among the Three Fires of the Leg, 66.12 Huo San can also strengthen the kidneys and treat lower back pain caused by kidney deficiency. Lee Kuo Cheng The Three Fires of the Leg (Zu San Huo) are highly effective for cardiovascular diseases and brain conditions, such as hydrocephalus, brain tumors, concussions, Parkinson's, stroke, heart attack, palpitations, dizziness, vertigo, tension headaches related to hypertension, and tinnitus. Yang Wei Chieh The Three Fires of the Leg help restore the connection between the kidneys and the heart. These points can strengthen the kidneys and alleviate lower back pain. According to Master Tung, Zu San Huo is contraindicated in pregnancy. However, Yang Wei Chieh suggests that only 66.12 Huo San is contraindicated. At the same time, 66.10 Huo Lian and 66.11 Huo Ju are permissible since they are located in the same positions as Sp-3 Tai Bai, Sp-4 Gong Sun, and Kid-2 Ran Guj which are considered safe for needling during pregnancy according to TCM texts. Chuan Min Wang A Case of Master Tung: Urticaria with underlying kidney fire excess, treated with bloodletting at DT.04 Wu Ling and needling 66.12 Huo San. The rash resolved after two treatments. Miriam Lee 66.12 Huo San can be used in elderly patients with one cold leg and one warm leg. Strengthen the cold side with 66.12 Huo San, remove the needle, and then disperse the warm side using 66.12 Huo San. Point Name Huö ['k] — Fire. Sån — Disperse. The point's name suggests its ability to treat disorders characterized by fire (Yang) in the upper part of the body.
